title: Green-Wood After Hours
description:
While we love the spirit of the Halloween season, Green-Wood remains an active cemetery. Out of respect for the grounds, masks and costumes are not permitted and guests wearing them will not be admitted on the tour.  



The dead don’t keep visiting hours, but we do! Join us after dark for a walk through Green-Wood’s history, legends, and secrets. And before you depart, step inside the Catacombs, a space that is normally locked to the public.   



 







Price: $30/24 for Members 




Get Tickets









Walking Tour(see details below)





BEFORE PURCHASING YOUR TICKET, PLEASE NOTE:




All ticket sales are final. Refunds are only permissible if the tour is canceled by Green-Wood. Tickets cannot be exchanged for a different tour date.  



Walking tour routes cover hilly, grassy, and uneven terrain which may be difficult to navigate. This tour is not ADA compliant and is not recommended for children under the age of 10. There is no place to sit down during the tour. We strongly encourage attendees to wear suitable footwear.  



This tour takes place in the dark. Attendees are strongly encouraged to bring a flashlight. Unless there is a medical emergency, it may be difficult to exit quickly during the tour. Please consider these limitations before purchasing tickets. 



Attendees must follow all instructions and guidance from Cemetery staff and volunteers. 



Feeling sick? Stay home if you are feeling sick or running a fever. 



Attendees assume all risk of injury, harm, or death, and agree to release, indemnify, defend, and forever discharge Green-Wood from all liability, claims, demands, damages, costs, expenses, and causes of action. 



By registering for this tour, you consent to be photographed, filmed, and/or otherwise recorded.

title: Crime and Catastrophe Trolley Tour
description:
Credit: Green-Wood Staff





Murders, shipwrecks, plane crashes, gangsters: Do we have your attention yet? This nail-biting trolley tour delves deep into some of the finest true crime and disaster stories that Green-Wood has to offer. You will learn about the mysterious death of famed mentalist Washington Irving Bishop (who was allegedly killed by autopsy), discover the headline-grabbing murder of notorious mob boss Umberto “Albert” Anastasia, hear the salacious tale of the Hall-Mills Murders, and much more.  



 





Price: $30/$24 for members. 






Get Tickets









Trolley Tour(see details below)

title: Discover Green-Wood Trolley Tour
description:
Credit: Green-Wood Staff





Hop on board our cozy, warm trolley for an expert-led tour of Green-Wood’s historic landscape and some of the Cemetery’s most intriguing permanent residents. Whether you’re a first-time visitor or a seasoned explorer, this is your chance to experience 478 acres of art, history, and nature. Walk in the footsteps of George Washington and his troops during the Battle of Brooklyn; visit the grave of Jean-Michel Basquiat, one of America’s greatest artists; and discover so much more!

title: Revolutionary Spirits
description:
Courtesy of Fort Hamilton Distillery





Delve into the storied past of distilled spirits in Brooklyn with Green-Wood and our neighbors at Fort Hamilton Distillery. The afternoon kicks off with a trolley tour of the Cemetery to discover influential figures of the Revolutionary War and distillers who made their mark on the young Republic. Afterward, the trolley heads to Fort Hamilton Distillery in Industry City where you’ll experience “white” rye straight off the still, sample whiskey directly from the barrel, and learn how to bottle your own spirits! You’ll get a tasting of four whiskeys, followed by a sampling of barrel-aged maple syrup. 





Price: $50, $45 for members 






Get Tickets









Trolley Tour(see details below)





Fort Hamilton Distillery started barreling whiskey in 2016 when founders Alex Clark and Amy Grindeland embarked on a mission to recapture America’s finest spirits. Based in Industry City, Brooklyn, just steps from the Cemetery, the distillery is surrounded by landmarks of the Revolutionary War, from which the whiskey maker draws his inspiration.

title: Uprising/Downfall: 250 Years of Courage, Repression, and Resistance on the Road to American Democracy
description: This teach-in, featuring artists, activists, advocates, writers, and scholars, will examine 20th century social movements that advanced democracy and human rights, and State activities that sought to repress them.

title: Grave Beginnings: Green-Wood By Trolley
description:
Credit: Maike Schulz





Discover Green-Wood’s stunning landscape and remarkable history on this free hour-long trolley tour. Perfect for first-time visitors, this accessible introduction takes you on a leisurely ride to hear about notable residents, including Auguste Renouard, the “Father of modern day embalming”; industrialist William Colgate, whose legacy extends far beyond soap; scientist John Draper, a pioneer in photography and chemistry; and more. The tour also highlights other influential individuals who contributed to the city’s cultural, scientific, and civic life. 



This tour series is funded by Simons Foundation International and administered by the Simons Foundation’s Science, Society & Culture division.

title: Green-Wood's Greatest Hits
description:
Whether it’s your first visit to Green-Wood or your hundredth, this walking tour offers a fresh perspective on one of New York City’s most iconic landmarks. 



Led by one of our expert guides, this tour takes you to the heart of Brooklyn’s most fascinating stories. Walk in the footsteps of George Washington’s troops during the fight for independence, uncover the tragic tale of the 1876 Brooklyn Theatre fire, and pay tribute to luminaries like composer Leonard Bernstein. Along the way, you’ll encounter hidden gems and learn about unforgettable moments that have shaped the city and its culture.

title: Catch the Colors: Fall at Green-Wood
description:

Autumn has arrived, and Green-Wood is ablaze with the vibrant hues of the season! Each year, the Cemetery transforms into a breathtaking canvas of fiery reds, oranges, and yellows as its thousands of trees showcase their seasonal splendor. Bring your camera, your curiosity, and your love of nature to this unforgettable exploration in one of Brooklyn’s most beautiful settings.

title: Toddler Takeover at the Green-House
description:
Move over, big kids! On Tuesday mornings, it’s toddler time at the Green-House. Bring your little ones to the most fun pop-up play zone in Sunset Park for a morning of open play and sensory exploration. Activity stations will vary for each program. Got a train enthusiast? They’ll love the Cemetery’s toy vehicles! A budding builder? Our foam mausoleum blocks are perfect for tiny architects. Junior scientists can interact with bug specimens, bird puppets, magnifying glasses, and more. 



Come hang out with fellow parents and caregivers while your children explore, create, and play. Don’t forget your strollers, snacks, and playful spirit!  





Price: Free 






Buy Tickets









In-Person Event(see details below)





Presented in partnership with Park Slope Parents



Please note that if only 1 ticket shows as available during the registration process, that is the last ticket available. 



Know Before You Go:




Tickets: Due to program popularity and limited space, registration is required. 



Recommended for ages 1 to 4 years old. All children must be accompanied by a caregiver. 



Where To Go: This program takes place at the Green-House (750 Fifth Avenue), near the Main Entrance on Fifth Avenue and 25th Street.  



Accessibility & Safety: The Green-House is ADA-accessible. If you need accommodations for any reason, please contact our staff before reserving tickets at 718-210-3080, ext. 1, or events@green-wood.com.

title: TGIF! Afterschool Story and Craft Hour
description:
Photo Credits: Aaron Pierce





Kick off the weekend with story time and crafts at Green-Wood! Presented in partnership with Brooklyn Public Library, these sessions are led by Kidsmobile Librarian Michaela Donahue, who brings wonderful book selections perfect for young readers. At every program, the Library’s Bookmobile will be parked right outside the Green-House from 2–3pm. After you check out books, come inside for stories and crafts from 3–4pm! It’s a perfect way to discover new favorites, spark imagination, and enjoy quality time together. Don’t have a library card yet? Sign up and get one on the spot!  



 







Price: Free 




Get Tickets









The Green-House(see details below)





BEFORE PURCHASING YOUR TICKET, PLEASE NOTE:




All children must be accompanied by an adult and all adults must be accompanied by a child to attend this program. 



Participation is free; registration is recommended so we can get a rough headcount.



Know Before You Go:



Tickets: No registration required. Drop in and join us. Seating and activities are first come, first served. 



Recommended for ages 2 to 5 years old. All children must be accompanied by a caregiver. 



Where To Go: This program takes place at the Green-House (750 Fifth Avenue), near the Main Entrance on Fifth Avenue and 25th Street.  



Accessibility & Safety: The Green-House is ADA-accessible. If you need accommodations for any reason, please contact our staff before reserving tickets at 718-768-7300 ext. 5, or events@green-wood.com. 



Adult caregivers must stay with children at all times. 



Green-Wood staff may photograph, film and/or otherwise record this program.  If you do not wish to be photographed or recorded, you must notify a Green-Wood staff member before the program begins.

title: Shaping LGBTQ+ History: A Family Tour and Workshop
description:
Credit: Green-Wood Staff





Green-Wood has partnered with History UnErased to bring families together to learn about LGBTQ+ historical figures memorialized at Green-Wood, then create their own clay art inspired by them. Together we’ll introduce families to queer representation in history and the arts, model age-appropriate conversations about LGBTQ+ identities, and give families a joyful way to express themselves through keepsakes they’ll treasure.  



First, board our trolley to visit the graves of sculptors, painters, composers, and more. Then head to the classroom to make your own keychain, earrings, pendant, or other clay trinket, guided by Green-Wood’s educators and History UnErased’s teaching artists.  



History UnErased is putting LGBTQ history in its rightful place — the classroom — and uniting all “We the People” with a more complete story of America. Since 2018, History UnErased has been working with NYC Public Schools with funding from the New York City Council.  



All materials will be provided and no experience with clay is necessary. Space is limited. Participants must reserve tickets.  



The content of this program will be aimed at children ages 5 and older and their families, but younger siblings are also welcome! Participants must have at least one child in their group and all children must be accompanied by an adult. Maximum of four children to one adult participant.

title: Birding In Peace
description:
Before our gates open to the public, this early morning walking tour provides exclusive access to discover the many birds that call Green-Wood home, at least temporarily.  



Stop by this fall and you will see a variety of species passing through. By September, the offspring of summer’s nesting birds will be on their own. Returning warblers will be in their less flamboyant fall plumage. Catch a glimpse of spot blackbirds, flycatchers, sparrows, vireos, and swallows on the move. By October, be on the lookout for returning waterfowl and raptors heading south. And by November, overwintering feathered denizens return from the north.

description:

Discover Green-Wood’s stunning landscape and remarkable history on this free 90-minute walking tour. title: Birding in Peace: Late-Risers Edition (Members Only)
description:
Photo Credit: Rob Jett





If you’ve always wanted to go on a birding tour at Green-Wood but aren’t much of a morning person, this tour is for you! The early bird-er might get the worm, but you can birdwatch at any hour. Join birding expert Rob Jett and a small group of fellow members to roam the grounds while hearing and seeing the many feathered friends of Green-Wood.    



You can expect to see different species on each tour. As temperatures fall, varieties of sparrows will return to Green-Wood to overwinter, including chipping sparrows, fox sparrows, and dark-eyed juncos. Many blackbirds, flycatchers, vireos, and swallows will stop over in our trees as well. During the latter half of fall, we may spot some vagrant species uncommon in the northeast, like the rare ash-throated flycatcher.

title: Fame, Fortune, & the Forgotten: The Untold Stories of Victorian Women
description:
Join us in celebration of the bold, defiant, and often overlooked women of the nineteenth century. We’re partnering with the Dead Ladies Show to explore the stories behind Charlotte Canda’s magnificent tomb, a monument to a life tragically cut short; the colorful adventures of Lola Montez, whose daring career as a dancer and courtesan captivated royalty; and Anna Leah Fox, a spiritualist at the heart of the Victorian séance craze. Along the way, discover other women who defied societal norms and shaped their times in unexpected ways.  Dead Ladies Show is a NYC and Berlin-based podcast and live storytelling event series that celebrates the lives, legacies, and lasting impact of remarkable women from history.

title: Tom at the Farm
description: ABOUTTom drives out from the city for his boyfriend's funeral and discovers the family never knew their son was gay. His brother intends to keep it that way. What grows between them is stranger than a standoff: threats that slide into tenderness, a grieving stranger pulled deeper into a family that will not let him leave or let him be known.Rodrigo Portella stages Michel Marc Bouchard's play on a ring of open earth that comes to stand for a whole country turning back on itself. Winner of the top prizes of the Brazilian stage, the production has built an acclaimed international trajectory, with performances in Montreal, Avignon, Paris, Brussels, a tour across France, Switzerland and Belgium, a successful season at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, and most recently in South Korea. It now makes its U.S. premiere at NYU Skirball on its way to London's Barbican.ADVISORY    This production features sexual content and nudity.  RUN TIME    Approximately 2 hours, no intermission  LANGUAGE    This production is performed in Portuguese with English subtitles.

title: Rimaqpanpa: Multilingual and Multidisciplinary Seminar on Andean Studies
description: This two-day, public Rimaqpanpa (https://as.nyu.edu/research-centers/clacs/events/fall-2026/rimaqpanpa-andean-studies-seminar-fall-2026.html)—a Quechua term meaning "platform of omens" or "esplanade of dialogues"—brings together 11 leading Andean scholars and artists from around the world, who will discuss and disseminate the groundbreaking scholarship that has shaped the field of Andean Studies over the last two decades.  This inaugural Rimaqpanpa also highlights the cultural riches of the Andean world, featuring the legendary Andean soprano Sylvia Falcón and the premiere of filmmaker Ramon Rivera-Moret's two short films about Andean sky observers.

title: Vitalisms II
description: Vitalisms II is an exhibition-as-experiment that continues a long-term research and education project on contemporary painting in China. Following the first chapter's inquiry into the historicity of painting, we now turn toward a different question: How does valuecome into being through our encounters with painting?  As the opening season of our new artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), Vitalisms II considers inheritance as a condition we inhabit and reinterpret. Within the financial imagination, value is rendered calculable, comparable, and exchangeable. Yet value can also name artistic, historical, social, institutional, and affective relations. What happens when a painting is encountered as an artwork, cultural artifact, collectible object, commodity, or financial asset?Vitalisms II focuses on abstract and non-representational painting, a field whose boundaries remain uncertain. The exhibition brings together practices ranging from conceptually driven, hard-edged geometric painting to more intuitive and expressive approaches, including works that approach the threshold of representation. How might abstraction reveal, rather than obscure, relations that are otherwise difficult to perceive? How might we keep interpretation open, rather than seeking settlement? And what might speculation come to mean as a practice of imagining otherwise, rather than predicting return?  The title Vitalisms draws from Isabelle Graw's account of painting's "vitalistic fantasies"—how vitality and agency have been projected onto painting. *Vitalisms I asked whether we could extend these fantasies and think of paintings as active participants in the historical and social relations through which they are made, encountered, and circulated. Vitalisms II asks: What might happen when we approach a painting not simply as an image to be interpreted, but as something with which we enter into relation?  Like the first Vitalisms, this chapter is conceived as an experiment in which knowledge is exchanged and produced throughout the exhibition. During weekly study sessions, we spend extended time with the paintings, developing interpretations collectively through close looking, discussion, and reflection. These encounters become part of the exhibition's research, inviting us to ask: What might we come to value—and, in turn, make possible?  * Isabelle Graw, The Love of Painting (Sternberg Press, 2018): 21-24.——————————————————���——————————————————–Vitalisms II is accompanied by related events, including:  OPENING RECEPTIONFriday, 18 September, 16:00–19:00        A public reception to celebrate the exhibition's opening with food and drinks.STUDY SESSION (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/form-and-content-ii)  Form & Content II: How Do We Value Painting(s)?Fridays, 13:00–14:00 (English) / 16:00–17:00 PM (Chinese)      9, 16, 23, 30 October      6, 13, 20 November        For the artwork featured in each session and the full schedule, please visit the event webpage.  A weekly series of Study Sessions facilitated by ICA curators using Visual Thinking Strategies (VTS). Each one-hour session focuses on a single painting, inviting participants to spend time looking and sharing their observations and interpretations through conversation. The sessions bring the public into Vitalisms II's research into how value comes into being through our encounters with painting. No prior knowledge of art or the exhibition is required.ROUNDTABLE (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/after-looking)  After Looking: What Does Looking Have to Do with Value?Saturday, 5 December, 13:30-17:00        A roundtable bringing together the artists exhibiting in Vitalisms II and the ICA curators who facilitated the exhibition's Study Sessions. Over seven weeks, the public spent sustained time with individual paintings through close looking and group discussion. From these sessions, the curators will bring selected observations, interpretations, and questions into conversation with the artists, exploring how paintings acquire meaning and value through different encounters.  All events are FREE and OPEN to the public.  For further details and to register for events, please visit the event pages under Related programs below.  —————————���———————————————————————��———–  The exhibition Vitalisms II and related events are presented as the first season of the ICA's artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), attending to what inheritance asks of us and how we might inhabit unfinished worlds through practices of interpretation, response, and transformation.Vitalisms II is organized by Michelle Yeonho Hyun with BAO Yang and CHEN Baichao, with additional support by HOU Chuchu, QU Yanqiu and JIAO Meiqi. Special thanks to Arts & Collections Foundation, Luoying Sheng, Han Xiao, and Chong Zhou for their generosity, as well as Antenna Space, CLC Gallery, Magician Space, Ota Fine Arts, ShanghART Gallery and ZIAN Gallery, for their support. Graphic Design by LIU Anqi. Exhibition Design by FANG Yuan.  Our deepest gratitude belongs to the artists for sharing their knowledge, work, and time with us, extending our curiosity and creating more questions.  Early research and development for Untimely Inheritances received kind support from Goethe-Institut, as well as research assistance from Oviya Dinakhar, Fay Guan, and Lizzy Xie.

title: Vitalisms II
description: Vitalisms II is an exhibition-as-experiment that continues a long-term research and education project on contemporary painting in China. Following the first chapter's inquiry into the historicity of painting, we now turn toward a different question: How does valuecome into being through our encounters with painting?  As the opening season of our new artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), Vitalisms II considers inheritance as a condition we inhabit and reinterpret. Within the financial imagination, value is rendered calculable, comparable, and exchangeable. Yet value can also name artistic, historical, social, institutional, and affective relations. What happens when a painting is encountered as an artwork, cultural artifact, collectible object, commodity, or financial asset?Vitalisms II focuses on abstract and non-representational painting, a field whose boundaries remain uncertain. The exhibition brings together practices ranging from conceptually driven, hard-edged geometric painting to more intuitive and expressive approaches, including works that approach the threshold of representation. How might abstraction reveal, rather than obscure, relations that are otherwise difficult to perceive? How might we keep interpretation open, rather than seeking settlement? And what might speculation come to mean as a practice of imagining otherwise, rather than predicting return?  The title Vitalisms draws from Isabelle Graw's account of painting's "vitalistic fantasies"—how vitality and agency have been projected onto painting. *Vitalisms I asked whether we could extend these fantasies and think of paintings as active participants in the historical and social relations through which they are made, encountered, and circulated. Vitalisms II asks: What might happen when we approach a painting not simply as an image to be interpreted, but as something with which we enter into relation?  Like the first Vitalisms, this chapter is conceived as an experiment in which knowledge is exchanged and produced throughout the exhibition. During weekly study sessions, we spend extended time with the paintings, developing interpretations collectively through close looking, discussion, and reflection. These encounters become part of the exhibition's research, inviting us to ask: What might we come to value—and, in turn, make possible?  * Isabelle Graw, The Love of Painting (Sternberg Press, 2018): 21-24.——————————————————���——————————————————–Vitalisms II is accompanied by related events, including:  OPENING RECEPTIONFriday, 18 September, 16:00–19:00        A public reception to celebrate the exhibition's opening with food and drinks.STUDY SESSION (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/form-and-content-ii)  Form & Content II: How Do We Value Painting(s)?Fridays, 13:00–14:00 (English) / 16:00–17:00 PM (Chinese)      9, 16, 23, 30 October      6, 13, 20 November        For the artwork featured in each session and the full schedule, please visit the event webpage.  A weekly series of Study Sessions facilitated by ICA curators using Visual Thinking Strategies (VTS). Each one-hour session focuses on a single painting, inviting participants to spend time looking and sharing their observations and interpretations through conversation. The sessions bring the public into Vitalisms II's research into how value comes into being through our encounters with painting. No prior knowledge of art or the exhibition is required.ROUNDTABLE (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/after-looking)  After Looking: What Does Looking Have to Do with Value?Saturday, 5 December, 13:30-17:00        A roundtable bringing together the artists exhibiting in Vitalisms II and the ICA curators who facilitated the exhibition's Study Sessions. Over seven weeks, the public spent sustained time with individual paintings through close looking and group discussion. From these sessions, the curators will bring selected observations, interpretations, and questions into conversation with the artists, exploring how paintings acquire meaning and value through different encounters.  All events are FREE and OPEN to the public.  For further details and to register for events, please visit the event pages under Related programs below.  —————————���———————————————————————��———–  The exhibition Vitalisms II and related events are presented as the first season of the ICA's artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), attending to what inheritance asks of us and how we might inhabit unfinished worlds through practices of interpretation, response, and transformation.Vitalisms II is organized by Michelle Yeonho Hyun with BAO Yang and CHEN Baichao, with additional support by HOU Chuchu, QU Yanqiu and JIAO Meiqi. Special thanks to Arts & Collections Foundation, Luoying Sheng, Han Xiao, and Chong Zhou for their generosity, as well as Antenna Space, CLC Gallery, Magician Space, Ota Fine Arts, ShanghART Gallery and ZIAN Gallery, for their support. Graphic Design by LIU Anqi. Exhibition Design by FANG Yuan.  Our deepest gratitude belongs to the artists for sharing their knowledge, work, and time with us, extending our curiosity and creating more questions.  Early research and development for Untimely Inheritances received kind support from Goethe-Institut, as well as research assistance from Oviya Dinakhar, Fay Guan, and Lizzy Xie.

title: Aging in Diverse Populations: Social Contexts, Health Outcomes, and Life Experiences
description: The Global Institute for Longevity and Resilience is hosting a seminar titled "Aging in Diverse Populations: Social Contexts, Health Outcomes, and Life Experiences."  Talk 1: Living Arrangements, Loneliness, and Cognitive Function in Older Asian and Latin American Adults    Speaker: Qian Song, Associate Professor & Undergraduate Program Director, Donna M and Robert J Manning College of Nursing and Health Sciences, University of Massachusetts Boston      Focusing on social forces as a fundamental cause of health inequities, three major themes define Dr. Song's scholarship. The first theme investigates migrants' lack of full citizenship rights in their migration destinations as a cause of various health disparities in late life. The second theme assesses the consequences of family living arrangements and adult migration for the health and well-being of families considered "left-behind" in migrant sending communities. The third theme examines the short- and long-term effects of job layoffs on various health outcomes and health behaviors.   Talk 2: The Many Faces of Aging in America: Immigrants, Minorities, and the Social Determinants of Health    Speaker: May Guo, Professor, School of Social Work, University of Iowa      May (Man) Guo, Ph.D., FGSA, is a Professor in the School of Social Work at the University of Iowa. Dr. Guo's research explores the intersection of immigration and aging, addressing a broad range of topics, including acculturation, family relations, social support, coping, resilience, and cognitive and mental health among older immigrants. By systematically investigating the social determinants of health at the individual, family, neighborhood, and societal levels among older immigrants, Dr. Guo's work seeks to enhance the rigor of aging theories, which have traditionally been grounded in studies of White, non-migrant populations. Her recent research focuses on the nexus of race/ethnicity and immigration status, exploring the diverse aging experiences and health outcomes of minority older adults. An advocate for advancing gerontological social work, Dr. Guo is dedicated to teaching, mentoring students, and fostering cross-disciplinary collaborations to address the challenges faced by diverse aging populations.      Each talk will be approximately 30 minutes. Followed by a Q&A session.  Introduction by: Bei Wu, Provost and Distinguished Global Professor of Public Health, NYU Shanghai  This event is open to the NYU Shanghai Community. You are encouraged to RSVP through here (https://engage.shanghai.nyu.edu/event/12809882), but walk-ins are also welcome. Light refreshments will be provided.

title: Faculty and Staff Luncheon with Casper ter Kuile
description: In the shifting landscape of education and technology, what we owe each other isn't always clear.  Join us for a faculty and staff luncheon with Casper ter Kuile, author of The Power of Ritual (https://www.harpercollins.com/products/the-power-of-ritual-casper-ter-kuile?variant=32894732140578) and GSL Scholar-in-Residence, to explore practical ways to honor our duty of care as educators and leaders, especially in the age of AI. Inspired by his forthcoming research on covenant relationships as spiritual technology, Casper draws on the wisdom of ancient traditions to help us determine what we owe each other in the modern world.  Lunch will be provided. Please note that this gathering is intended for NYU faculty and staff.

title: Unwind in Color at the NEST
Vitalisms II
description: Vitalisms II is an exhibition-as-experiment that continues a long-term research and education project on contemporary painting in China. Following the first chapter's inquiry into the historicity of painting, we now turn toward a different question: How does valuecome into being through our encounters with painting?  As the opening season of our new artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), Vitalisms II considers inheritance as a condition we inhabit and reinterpret. Within the financial imagination, value is rendered calculable, comparable, and exchangeable. Yet value can also name artistic, historical, social, institutional, and affective relations. What happens when a painting is encountered as an artwork, cultural artifact, collectible object, commodity, or financial asset?Vitalisms II focuses on abstract and non-representational painting, a field whose boundaries remain uncertain. The exhibition brings together practices ranging from conceptually driven, hard-edged geometric painting to more intuitive and expressive approaches, including works that approach the threshold of representation. How might abstraction reveal, rather than obscure, relations that are otherwise difficult to perceive? How might we keep interpretation open, rather than seeking settlement? And what might speculation come to mean as a practice of imagining otherwise, rather than predicting return?  The title Vitalisms draws from Isabelle Graw's account of painting's "vitalistic fantasies"—how vitality and agency have been projected onto painting. *Vitalisms I asked whether we could extend these fantasies and think of paintings as active participants in the historical and social relations through which they are made, encountered, and circulated. Vitalisms II asks: What might happen when we approach a painting not simply as an image to be interpreted, but as something with which we enter into relation?  Like the first Vitalisms, this chapter is conceived as an experiment in which knowledge is exchanged and produced throughout the exhibition. During weekly study sessions, we spend extended time with the paintings, developing interpretations collectively through close looking, discussion, and reflection. These encounters become part of the exhibition's research, inviting us to ask: What might we come to value—and, in turn, make possible?  * Isabelle Graw, The Love of Painting (Sternberg Press, 2018): 21-24.——————————————————���——————————————————–Vitalisms II is accompanied by related events, including:  OPENING RECEPTIONFriday, 18 September, 16:00–19:00        A public reception to celebrate the exhibition's opening with food and drinks.STUDY SESSION (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/form-and-content-ii)  Form & Content II: How Do We Value Painting(s)?Fridays, 13:00–14:00 (English) / 16:00–17:00 PM (Chinese)      9, 16, 23, 30 October      6, 13, 20 November        For the artwork featured in each session and the full schedule, please visit the event webpage.  A weekly series of Study Sessions facilitated by ICA curators using Visual Thinking Strategies (VTS). Each one-hour session focuses on a single painting, inviting participants to spend time looking and sharing their observations and interpretations through conversation. The sessions bring the public into Vitalisms II's research into how value comes into being through our encounters with painting. No prior knowledge of art or the exhibition is required.ROUNDTABLE (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/after-looking)  After Looking: What Does Looking Have to Do with Value?Saturday, 5 December, 13:30-17:00        A roundtable bringing together the artists exhibiting in Vitalisms II and the ICA curators who facilitated the exhibition's Study Sessions. Over seven weeks, the public spent sustained time with individual paintings through close looking and group discussion. From these sessions, the curators will bring selected observations, interpretations, and questions into conversation with the artists, exploring how paintings acquire meaning and value through different encounters.  All events are FREE and OPEN to the public.  For further details and to register for events, please visit the event pages under Related programs below.  —————————���———————————————————————��———–  The exhibition Vitalisms II and related events are presented as the first season of the ICA's artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), attending to what inheritance asks of us and how we might inhabit unfinished worlds through practices of interpretation, response, and transformation.Vitalisms II is organized by Michelle Yeonho Hyun with BAO Yang and CHEN Baichao, with additional support by HOU Chuchu, QU Yanqiu and JIAO Meiqi. Special thanks to Arts & Collections Foundation, Luoying Sheng, Han Xiao, and Chong Zhou for their generosity, as well as Antenna Space, CLC Gallery, Magician Space, Ota Fine Arts, ShanghART Gallery and ZIAN Gallery, for their support. Graphic Design by LIU Anqi. Exhibition Design by FANG Yuan.  Our deepest gratitude belongs to the artists for sharing their knowledge, work, and time with us, extending our curiosity and creating more questions.  Early research and development for Untimely Inheritances received kind support from Goethe-Institut, as well as research assistance from Oviya Dinakhar, Fay Guan, and Lizzy Xie.

title: The Culture of Purpose - Book Talk
description: Join us for a conversation about purpose, trust, and leadership in the age of AI.RSVP HERE (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdO_Jt15SCVAeJjQmI2B5URZYIM3FfQpeilpkBiIV-tZSe4zw/viewform)  The NYU SPS Division of Programs in Business (DPB) invites the NYU community to a conversation with Pascal Wiscour-Conter, author of The Culture of Purpose: How to Communicate in the Age of Intelligence.  As part of DPB's Industry Connection Series, Wiscour-Conter will explore how leaders can use storytelling to shape culture, build trust, and help people navigate uncertainty. In an AI-driven world overflowing with content, being heard takes more than speaking louder. Drawing on three years of interdisciplinary research, his book offers a practical framework for communicating with purpose, connecting with audiences, and using AI to strengthen human creativity and judgment.Pascal Wiscour-Conter is an international entrepreneur, advisor, and author whose career spans finance, maritime entrepreneurship, and the entertainment industry. title: Advancing Disaster Risk Reduction in a Changing World: Lessons Learned from the Past in the U.S. and Japan—and Investments for the Future
description: The need for competent disaster management continues to increase. In 2023, the estimated economic loss of natural disasters worldwide was 380 billion USD, with another 118 billion USD in insured losses. Increased need paired with scarce resources and inefficiencies in the current response landscape will require improved solutions that are responsive to local needs and drive capacity-building.  The U.S. and Japan are uncontested leaders in disaster risk reduction (DRR) and have similar risk profiles so peer-to-peer learning would be valuable to decisionmakers in both countries. Despite having robust systems, both the U.S. and Japan face persistent gaps in local-level capacity, public-private coordination, and the integration of innovation into resilience planning that affect their economic competitiveness and investment profile.  Two recent anniversaries—20 years since Hurricane Katrina (August 29, 2025) and 15 years since the 3/11 Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami disaster (March 11, 2026), the second and most costly disasters in economic losses respectively since 1900 —offered an opportunity to reflect on progress and chart a forward-looking agenda. What have we learned since those watershed moments and what lessons can be gleaned for policymakers as they work to incentivize locally-led community action, and especially private sector-led investment, over the next 20 years? What do decisionmakers need to prioritize to improve resilience and future-proof investments?  Chloe Demrovsky will present the preliminary findings from her research project in partnership with Rui Kotani and Toshiya Hoshino from the University of Osaka and generously supported by the US-Japan Foundation.

title: Chattel Like Cattle: Enslaved Women as Perfect Property
description: CSAAD 2026-2027 Distinguished Scholar EventSir Hilary Beckles, Vice ChancellorThe University of the West IndiesTuesday, October 13, 20265:30 pm – 7:00 pmNYU Silver Center, Hemmerdinger Hall31 Washington PlNew York City, NY 10003Zoom link: https://nyu.zoom.us/j/93841506438The 'West' broke away from traditional forms of enslavement and invented an entirely new and unprecedented system that was chattel slavery. It was designed specifically for Africans who were legally classified as non-human. They were defined as property with all the features of chattel. They could be bought, sold, mortgaged, bequeathed, used as currency, and were taxable. As non-humans they could be raped, prostituted, and provided socio-sexual services. African women were placed at the center of the Chattel system. It was through the black woman that the model became inter-generational with the market agreement of her fertility and maternity. Her experience was therefore significantly different from that of the African male. This lecture sets out how it was done across colonial Americas.Bio:The Vice Chancellor of The University of the West Indies, Sir Hilary Beckles is a distinguished academic, international thought leader, United Nations committee official, and global public activist in the field of social justice and minority empowerment.Educated at the University of Hull, Sir Hilary is a Director of SAGICOR Financial Corporation, the  largest financial company in the Caribbean region, Chairman of the Caribbean Examinations Council, former Chairman of The University of the West Indies Press, Chairman of the Caribbean  Community (CARICOM), Commission on Reparation and Social Justice, former President of Universities Caribbean, an editor of the UNESCO General History of Africa series and a Director  of the Global Tourism Resilience and Crisis Management Centre. He has also served as an advisor  to the UN World Culture Report and Advisor to the Secretary General of the United Nations on  Sustainable Development. He is a past Vice President of the International Task Force for the UNESCO Slave Route Project and a past consultant for the UNESCO Cities for Peace Global Programme. He sits on the Council of the Association of Commonwealth Universities and is also Chancellor of the United Nations University.Sir Beckles has Honorary Doctorate Awards from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and  Technology, Hull University, Brock University, University of Glasgow, the University of  Johannesburg, North-West University, and the University of London. Sir Hilary Beckles is also the  recipient of the prestigious Sir Martin Luther King Jr Award for global advocacy, academic  scholarship and intellectual leadership in support of social justice, institutional equity, and  economic development for marginalized and oppressed ethnicities and nations.*This event is cosponsored by New York University Center for Latin American and Caribbean Studies*For accommodations, please contact the Assistant Director for the Center for the Study of Africa and the African Diaspora at ac8829@nyu.edu.Register Here

title: The Art of the Fold at the NEST
Vitalisms II
description: Vitalisms II is an exhibition-as-experiment that continues a long-term research and education project on contemporary painting in China. Following the first chapter's inquiry into the historicity of painting, we now turn toward a different question: How does valuecome into being through our encounters with painting?  As the opening season of our new artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), Vitalisms II considers inheritance as a condition we inhabit and reinterpret. Within the financial imagination, value is rendered calculable, comparable, and exchangeable. Yet value can also name artistic, historical, social, institutional, and affective relations. What happens when a painting is encountered as an artwork, cultural artifact, collectible object, commodity, or financial asset?Vitalisms II focuses on abstract and non-representational painting, a field whose boundaries remain uncertain. The exhibition brings together practices ranging from conceptually driven, hard-edged geometric painting to more intuitive and expressive approaches, including works that approach the threshold of representation. How might abstraction reveal, rather than obscure, relations that are otherwise difficult to perceive? How might we keep interpretation open, rather than seeking settlement? And what might speculation come to mean as a practice of imagining otherwise, rather than predicting return?  The title Vitalisms draws from Isabelle Graw's account of painting's "vitalistic fantasies"—how vitality and agency have been projected onto painting. *Vitalisms I asked whether we could extend these fantasies and think of paintings as active participants in the historical and social relations through which they are made, encountered, and circulated. Vitalisms II asks: What might happen when we approach a painting not simply as an image to be interpreted, but as something with which we enter into relation?  Like the first Vitalisms, this chapter is conceived as an experiment in which knowledge is exchanged and produced throughout the exhibition. During weekly study sessions, we spend extended time with the paintings, developing interpretations collectively through close looking, discussion, and reflection. These encounters become part of the exhibition's research, inviting us to ask: What might we come to value—and, in turn, make possible?  * Isabelle Graw, The Love of Painting (Sternberg Press, 2018): 21-24.——————————————————���——————————————————–Vitalisms II is accompanied by related events, including:  OPENING RECEPTIONFriday, 18 September, 16:00–19:00        A public reception to celebrate the exhibition's opening with food and drinks.STUDY SESSION (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/form-and-content-ii)  Form & Content II: How Do We Value Painting(s)?Fridays, 13:00–14:00 (English) / 16:00–17:00 PM (Chinese)      9, 16, 23, 30 October      6, 13, 20 November        For the artwork featured in each session and the full schedule, please visit the event webpage.  A weekly series of Study Sessions facilitated by ICA curators using Visual Thinking Strategies (VTS). Each one-hour session focuses on a single painting, inviting participants to spend time looking and sharing their observations and interpretations through conversation. The sessions bring the public into Vitalisms II's research into how value comes into being through our encounters with painting. No prior knowledge of art or the exhibition is required.ROUNDTABLE (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/after-looking)  After Looking: What Does Looking Have to Do with Value?Saturday, 5 December, 13:30-17:00        A roundtable bringing together the artists exhibiting in Vitalisms II and the ICA curators who facilitated the exhibition's Study Sessions. Over seven weeks, the public spent sustained time with individual paintings through close looking and group discussion. From these sessions, the curators will bring selected observations, interpretations, and questions into conversation with the artists, exploring how paintings acquire meaning and value through different encounters.  All events are FREE and OPEN to the public.  For further details and to register for events, please visit the event pages under Related programs below.  —————————���———————————————————————��———–  The exhibition Vitalisms II and related events are presented as the first season of the ICA's artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), attending to what inheritance asks of us and how we might inhabit unfinished worlds through practices of interpretation, response, and transformation.Vitalisms II is organized by Michelle Yeonho Hyun with BAO Yang and CHEN Baichao, with additional support by HOU Chuchu, QU Yanqiu and JIAO Meiqi. Special thanks to Arts & Collections Foundation, Luoying Sheng, Han Xiao, and Chong Zhou for their generosity, as well as Antenna Space, CLC Gallery, Magician Space, Ota Fine Arts, ShanghART Gallery and ZIAN Gallery, for their support. Graphic Design by LIU Anqi. Exhibition Design by FANG Yuan.  Our deepest gratitude belongs to the artists for sharing their knowledge, work, and time with us, extending our curiosity and creating more questions.  Early research and development for Untimely Inheritances received kind support from Goethe-Institut, as well as research assistance from Oviya Dinakhar, Fay Guan, and Lizzy Xie.

title: Choosing Reliable Sources : How Do You Know? Let's Get Critical: Arts & Humanities Research Day
description: In our current information landscape, it can be hard to know if something is "real" or "fake." An alternative strategy is to reframe the question as "Is this a reliable source?" This strategy for determining which sources to use in your research can make your life easier and your scholarship stronger. title: Screening of "Billi il cowboy"
description: It is the late 1960s, and in the Roman countryside, next to the construction sites of the burgeoning working-class suburbs, dozens of western films were being shot. Billi is twelve years old; she rides horses and dreams of being a cowboy. When a casting agent shows up looking for young extras to do some stunt work, Billi knows this is her big chance. Her family, however, thinks otherwise.  (Drama, 15', Italy, 2024)DIRECTOR'S NOTE  Cowboy Billi is about a precise moment in life: the end of childhood. Most children leave certain things behind and gain others, but for Billi, a kid whose true gender identity has lived safely inside the game of 'playing cowboy,' growing up threatens to take away a large part of who this kid is. Moving beyond the binary of conforming or rebelling, the film sets out to show the power of a free spirit and of self-determination.  Fede Gianni (b. 1986) is a trans screenwriter and director whose work has garnered international acclaim. His short films have been screened at prestigious international festivals and have earned awards from the Directors Guild of America, Vimeo, and The Gotham (formerly known as IFP). His latest short film, "Cowboy Billi," premiered at the 39th Critic's Week at the Venice International Film Festival. The feature-length expansion of "Cowboy Billi" has been selected for the 2025 Ikusmira Berriak residency at the San Sebastian Film Festival. In addition to his filmmaking, Gianni teaches film at John Cabot University in Rome and New York University in Florence.

title: Grad Student Lightning Talks: Let's Get Critical: Arts & Humanities Research Day: How Do You Know?
description: Our rapidly evolving information ecosystem demands that all researchers—and, perhaps, especially grad students—review and adjust their research methods in response to questions such as: How do we find, trace, and use citations in the era of AI hallucinations? To what and whom do we grant authority in a time marked by mis- and disinformation from figures and institutions previously regarded as relatively reliable? How might the particularities of the current publication landscape (ranging from the use of published scholarly writing to train language learning models to an increasing emphasis on open access) shape how and for whom we write?The Let's Get Critical: Art and Humanities Research Day graduate student lightning talks present Masters and Doctoral students in the arts and humanities at NYU with an opportunity to engage with these and similar questions in relation to their own work. This event also gives grad students an opportunity to actively contribute to interdisciplinary discussions about research methods in the current information landscape.The work of four current graduate students will be selected for presentation. Each speaker will be allotted ten minutes followed by a moderated panel discussion and Q&A.NYU Libraries is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. title: An American Miseducation: A Talk with Journalist/Writer Mara Marques Cavallaro
description: Join writer, reporter, and translator Mara Marques Cavallaro (https://www.maracavallaro.com/) for An American Miseducation, a talk exploring playful and innovative approaches to writing about gravely serious subjects. Centered on an essay, the session will examine the work's form and content and invite participants to put these ideas into practice through an exercise.  Based in New York City, Cavallaro has reported on inhumane conditions in ICE detention, police violence, immigration, environmental racism, underground abortion networks, and the legacies of Latin American dictatorships. Her work has appeared in The Nation, El Tecolote, and Jacobin. She is the Director of the Incarcerated Writers Initiative at Columbia University School of the Arts and the editor of its annual anthology, Exchange.

title: LSWSO Presents: Quiten sus Penas! (Take your worries away)
ISAW Exhibition Lecture: I Call Upon You, Gods of the Night: Protecting against Witchcraft and Demons in Mesopotamia
description: Registration is required. Please fill out the form at the bottom of this page.  The ancient Mesopotamian world was populated with a wide range of demonic and monstrous creatures, all of which intersected with daily life in a variety of mostly-malignant ways. Most often, demons, or the chaotic figure of the witch, could cause serious harm, being associated with disease and illness, or even death, particularly in infants and young children. But these forces could also be responsible for more mundane ills, with even a run of bad luck being attributable to witchcraft. This talk will discuss some of the major threats found in Mesopotamia—the demonic, chaotic witch; the demoness Lamashtu, who was often responsible for infant mortality; and others—examining in detail how they could be safeguarded against, or actively opposed once they were believed to be present. Mesopotamian ritual practices offered a range of possible options, from the exhaustively (and expensively) detailed to simpler, even mass-produced, remedies.  Gina Konstantopoulos (PhD, University of Michigan, 2015) is an Associate Professor in Assyriology and Cuneiform Studies in the Department of Near Eastern Languages and Cultures at UCLA. Her research centers on religion, magic, and literature in Mesopotamia, with a focus on the role of demons and monsters. Her monograph on this topic, The Divine/Demonic Seven and the Place of Demons in Mesopotamia, was published in 2023 by Brill. Her current research focuses on two major projects: one on the creation of distant and imagined lands and notions of space and place in the ancient Near East, and another on the works of Enheduana and Sumerian myths of Inana.  This talk is given in conjunction with ISAW's exhibition Cursed! The Power of Magic in the Ancient World. The exhibition is organized by the Toledo Museum of Art; its presentation at ISAW is made possible by generous support from the Gladys Krieble Delmas Foundation and the Leon Levy Foundation.Please check isaw.nyu.edu (https://isaw.nyu.edu/) for event updates.ISAW is committed to providing a positive and educational experience for all guests and participants who attend our public programming. We ask that all attendees follow the guidelines listed in our community standards policy (https://isaw.nyu.edu/events/community-standards-policy).

title: Vitalisms II
description: Vitalisms II is an exhibition-as-experiment that continues a long-term research and education project on contemporary painting in China. Following the first chapter's inquiry into the historicity of painting, we now turn toward a different question: How does valuecome into being through our encounters with painting?  As the opening season of our new artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), Vitalisms II considers inheritance as a condition we inhabit and reinterpret. Within the financial imagination, value is rendered calculable, comparable, and exchangeable. Yet value can also name artistic, historical, social, institutional, and affective relations. What happens when a painting is encountered as an artwork, cultural artifact, collectible object, commodity, or financial asset?Vitalisms II focuses on abstract and non-representational painting, a field whose boundaries remain uncertain. The exhibition brings together practices ranging from conceptually driven, hard-edged geometric painting to more intuitive and expressive approaches, including works that approach the threshold of representation. How might abstraction reveal, rather than obscure, relations that are otherwise difficult to perceive? How might we keep interpretation open, rather than seeking settlement? And what might speculation come to mean as a practice of imagining otherwise, rather than predicting return?  The title Vitalisms draws from Isabelle Graw's account of painting's "vitalistic fantasies"—how vitality and agency have been projected onto painting. *Vitalisms I asked whether we could extend these fantasies and think of paintings as active participants in the historical and social relations through which they are made, encountered, and circulated. Vitalisms II asks: What might happen when we approach a painting not simply as an image to be interpreted, but as something with which we enter into relation?  Like the first Vitalisms, this chapter is conceived as an experiment in which knowledge is exchanged and produced throughout the exhibition. During weekly study sessions, we spend extended time with the paintings, developing interpretations collectively through close looking, discussion, and reflection. These encounters become part of the exhibition's research, inviting us to ask: What might we come to value—and, in turn, make possible?  * Isabelle Graw, The Love of Painting (Sternberg Press, 2018): 21-24.——————————————————���——————————————————–Vitalisms II is accompanied by related events, including:  OPENING RECEPTIONFriday, 18 September, 16:00–19:00        A public reception to celebrate the exhibition's opening with food and drinks.STUDY SESSION (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/form-and-content-ii)  Form & Content II: How Do We Value Painting(s)?Fridays, 13:00–14:00 (English) / 16:00–17:00 PM (Chinese)      9, 16, 23, 30 October      6, 13, 20 November        For the artwork featured in each session and the full schedule, please visit the event webpage.  A weekly series of Study Sessions facilitated by ICA curators using Visual Thinking Strategies (VTS). Each one-hour session focuses on a single painting, inviting participants to spend time looking and sharing their observations and interpretations through conversation. The sessions bring the public into Vitalisms II's research into how value comes into being through our encounters with painting. No prior knowledge of art or the exhibition is required.ROUNDTABLE (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/after-looking)  After Looking: What Does Looking Have to Do with Value?Saturday, 5 December, 13:30-17:00        A roundtable bringing together the artists exhibiting in Vitalisms II and the ICA curators who facilitated the exhibition's Study Sessions. Over seven weeks, the public spent sustained time with individual paintings through close looking and group discussion. From these sessions, the curators will bring selected observations, interpretations, and questions into conversation with the artists, exploring how paintings acquire meaning and value through different encounters.  All events are FREE and OPEN to the public.  For further details and to register for events, please visit the event pages under Related programs below.  —————————���———————————————————————��———–  The exhibition Vitalisms II and related events are presented as the first season of the ICA's artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), attending to what inheritance asks of us and how we might inhabit unfinished worlds through practices of interpretation, response, and transformation.Vitalisms II is organized by Michelle Yeonho Hyun with BAO Yang and CHEN Baichao, with additional support by HOU Chuchu, QU Yanqiu and JIAO Meiqi. Special thanks to Arts & Collections Foundation, Luoying Sheng, Han Xiao, and Chong Zhou for their generosity, as well as Antenna Space, CLC Gallery, Magician Space, Ota Fine Arts, ShanghART Gallery and ZIAN Gallery, for their support. Graphic Design by LIU Anqi. Exhibition Design by FANG Yuan.  Our deepest gratitude belongs to the artists for sharing their knowledge, work, and time with us, extending our curiosity and creating more questions.  Early research and development for Untimely Inheritances received kind support from Goethe-Institut, as well as research assistance from Oviya Dinakhar, Fay Guan, and Lizzy Xie.

title: How Stringent Are Minimum Plot Size Regulations in Sub-Saharan Africa?: Involving Undergraduates in Cutting-Edge Research
description: ​Schedule  ​9:15-9:30 Light breakfast  ​9:30-9:35 Welcome: Interim Director Kari Kohn  ​9:35-9:40 Course and research background: Health, Environment and Policy Director Kevin Cromar  ​9:40-10:00 Presentation: Urban Expansion Director Solly Angel, Marron Fellow Simon De Boeck, and NYU undergraduate student Ceci Rodriguez  ​10:00-10:15 Q&A  ​10:15-10:30 Networking  ​About the NYU Marron Institute of Urban Management  ​The NYU Marron Institute conducts innovative applied research, working with cities to take on critical challenges of urban living. Started with a generous gift from Donald B. Marron, faculty members develop their programs, hire research staff and build portfolios of externally-funded projects that have the potential to improve outcomes in cities. Currently, the Marron Institute has six major research programs focused on urban planning (http://marroninstitute.nyu.edu/programs/urban-expansion?utm_source=luma), environmental health (http://marroninstitute.nyu.edu/programs/air-quality?utm_source=luma), civic analytics (https://marroninstitute.nyu.edu/programs/civic-analytics?utm_source=luma), transportation and land use (https://marroninstitute.nyu.edu/programs/transportation-and-land-use?utm_source=luma), human trafficking (https://marroninstitute.nyu.edu/programs/human-exploitation-and-resilience?utm_source=luma), and public sector performance and innovation (http://marroninstitute.nyu.edu/programs/litmus?utm_source=luma).  ​Globally, cities are home to more than half of the world's population—4 billion people and growing. Though the researchers and faculty members at the Marron Institute do publish and teach on occasion, their chief focus is the pursuit of sponsored research that will extend the impact of the Institute's founding gift and have a positive and measurable impact on life in cities the world over.  ​​Visitor Information  ​This event will be hosted in LC 400, located on the 4th Floor of 5 MetroTech in downtown Brooklyn, easily accessible from Jay St-MetroTech subway station. Advance registration through Luma is required for building access.

title: Pontormo and the Florentine Tradition: Nostalgia during the Siege of Florence
description: Studying the works of artists of previous generations was an essential part of an artist's formation in Renaissance Florence. Jacopo Pontormo (1494-1557) was no exception to this rule and demonstrated unusual sensitivity to the Florentine tradition throughout his career. However, Pontormo created some of his most important works during the period of the last Florentine republic and the dramatic siege that brought this short-lived political experiment to an end (1527-1530). Both the preparations of the Florentines for their defense and the ensuing siege brought significant destruction to both public and private buildings and, as a result, to the artworks that they contained. Under these trying circumstances, Pontormo appears to have paid even closer attention to Medieval and earlier Renaissance precedents. In this talk, I will consider what occasioned this increased attention to the art of the past and what its significance may have been for Pontormo and his contemporaries in Florence.

title: When the Horrors of War Meet the Power of Literature: Reactions and Transformations
description: This book is an initiative of the The Parents Circle – Families Forum (PCFF), edited by Sarai Shavit with fellow writer and literary editor Dr. Rawya Burbara. This is a multilingual anthology of short stories written by authors from both sides of the Israeli-Palestinian divide, addressing how contemporary Arab and Hebrew literature from both sides of the fence responds, clashes, and evolves in a contemporary geopolitical crisis as war. It tells the complex story of authors who collaborated on a joint artistic project before the war, and whose personal lives and creative work changed deeply after October 7th. The anthology offers a rare testimony to the power of art and humanity in such harsh and brutal times.

title: Nihongo Table: Movie Night
description: Experience Japanese language and culture through film at Nihongo Table: Movie Night! Join fellow students for a screening of a Japanese film followed by casual discussion and cultural exchange in a welcoming and supportive environment. Whether you're a beginner or an advanced speaker, this is a great opportunity to strengthen your listening skills, learn new vocabulary in context, and engage with Japanese culture through cinema. Share your thoughts, ask questions, and connect with other Japanese language learners while enjoying a movie together. All language levels are welcome!Who: Japanese language learners of all levels and anyone interested in Japanese film, language, and culture.Featured Film: After Life (1998)Synopsis: In this acclaimed Japanese film, a group of people who have recently died find themselves in a limbo realm resembling a relatively mundane building. Counselors, including Takashi (Arata) and Shiori (Erika Oda), are on hand to help new arrivals pick one memory from their lives to bring with them into eternity. Once the memories are chosen, the staff makes a short film representing each one, and the films make up a collage of thoughtful cinematic moments.Subtitles will be provided.Hosted by: Department of East Asian StudiesAdditional Information can be found at: https://engage.nyu.edu/event/12480836 (https://engage.nyu.edu/event/12480836)

title: The Score: Sports Betting's Grip on College Students
description: NYU Liberal Studies, NYU Athletics, and the Office of Student-Athlete Excellence are hosting The Score: Sports Betting's Grip on College Students, featuring a conversation with sports business, law, and society expert,Kenneth L. Shropshire (https://www.kennethshropshire.com/). He will be joined byRyan Westman (https://gonyuathletics.com/staff-directory/ryan-westman/504), NYU's director of academic and student-athlete support services and compliance officer, andMalik Williams (https://gonyuathletics.com/staff-directory/malik-williams/673)(LAW '19), NYU's associate director of athletics for compliance, who will act as moderators.This discussion will draw on perspectives from scholarship, sports competition, law, and business. They will explore how sports betting has become rampant—including who is impacted, who benefits, and insights on the way forward.Doors Open at 5:30 p.m. Program will be 6:00–7:30 p.m. Refreshments will be served.Open to the NYU community and the general public. Visitors must RSVP in advance and have a valid government ID to enter the building.RSVP Below to AttendAbout Kenneth L. ShropshireKenneth L. Shropshire (https://www.kennethshropshire.com/) is the David W. Hauck Professor Emeritus of Legal Studies and Business Ethics at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania and Professor Emeritus of Africana Studies. His scholarship and professional work explore the intersections of sports business, law, and race, as well as the opportunities and responsibilities educational institutions have toward athletes.              He is the coauthor, with Collin D. Williams, Jr., of The Miseducation of the Student-Athlete: How to Fix College Sports, recently reissued with a new preface examining the evolving landscape of college athletics. His other related books include In Black and White, Sport Matters, and The Business of Sports Agents.              Shropshire founded the Wharton Sports Business Initiative and later established and led the Global Sport Institute at Arizona State University. He currently serves as a Strategic Advisor to SeventySix Capital and as Lead Independent Director of Moelis & Company. A graduate of Stanford University and Columbia Law School, he began his career in private law practice and later worked with the Los Angeles Olympic Organizing Committee.      About Ryan WestmanRyan Westman (https://gonyuathletics.com/staff-directory/ryan-westman/504) serves as Director of Academic and Student-Athlete Support Services at New York University, where he supports the academic, leadership, and personal development of student-athletes and serves as sport advisor for baseball, wrestling, and men's and women's cross country and track & field.              He joined NYU in 2018 after nearly seven years at Seton Hall University, where he advised student-athletes across multiple sports and served as a mentor in the Freshman Studies Program.              Outside of his administrative work at NYU, Westman teaches courses on Intercollegiate Athletics at NYU Steinhardt in the Higher Education and Student Affairs (HESA) program and in the School of Professional Studies (SPS) Sports Business program.              A 2006 graduate of Rutgers University, Westman competed in track & field for four years and served as a captain of the program's first BIG EAST and IC4A championship teams. He was inducted into the Rutgers Athletics Hall of Fame in 2017. Westman earned his Ph.D. in Higher Education Leadership, Management and Policy from Seton Hall University in 2018. His doctoral research examined the impact of NCAA policies and programs on Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and Limited Resource Institutions competing in Division I athletics.      About Malik WilliamsMalik Williams (https://gonyuathletics.com/staff-directory/malik-williams/673) is in his fourth year as an Associate Director of Athletics at New York University. Malik plays a key role in the Department's strategic and financial planning while overseeing its NCAA compliance operation. He also provides sport oversight for several varsity programs: Men's Basketball, Men's and Women's Swimming, Men's and Women's Cross Country/Track & Field, and Baseball.              Prior to joining NYU Athletics, Malik worked as an Associate Attorney at Winston & Strawn LLP in the firm's Antitrust and Sports Litigation practice. During his time at Winston, he represented a number of high-profile clients, including Ben Simmons, Division I student-athletes, the NFL Players Association, Relevant Sports Group, and Activision Blizzard.              Malik is an alumnus of NYU School of Law, where he earned his J.D. in May 2019.         Note on Accessibility: It is a priority to make our events inclusive and accessible. The entrance of 708 Broadway and the 3rd Floor are accessible via elevator. For any questions or to notify us of accommodation requests, please emaillsdeansoffice@nyu.eduat least two weeks prior to the event date.

title: Listening from the Heart: An Evening with Peacemakers
description: Sima Awad and Maayan Inon have both lost a close family member to violence and are committed to working with "the other side" for nonviolence, reconciliation, and a just peace. They will be in conversation moderated by actor, comedian, and NYU alum Alex Edelman (CAS '12). Following their presentation, the audience is invited to stay for conversation circles to dig deeper about Israel, Palestine, and our shared humanity. Refreshments will be served.Please RSVP by October 9.  NYU in Dialogue is a series of events designed to grow our capacity to listen, to value different perspectives, and to flourish. The series brings together great minds from across our University and guests from around the world to stimulate thoughtful conversations about the pressing issues of the day.The Parents Circle – Families Forum (PCFF) is a joint Israeli-Palestinian organization of over 900 families, all of whom have lost an immediate family member to the ongoing conflict. The members have undertaken a joint effort amid ongoing and escalating violence to transform their loss and pain into a public and collective demand for peace and reconciliation. When those who have paid the highest personal price for the conflict publicly reject the logic of endless war, they challenge dominant narratives of inevitability, revenge and dehumanization.

title: Manual Cinema: The 4th Witch
description: ABOUT  Cameras roll, hands reach in, a shadow becomes a forest, a scrap of cardboard becomes a castle. You watch the movie get made. On a table full of overhead projectors, paper puppets, and tiny sets, the artists of Manual Cinema build Macbeth shot by shot in front of you, and a finished film assembles itself on the screen above. Immersive sound design and an original score are played live.  The story starts where Shakespeare's play ends. A girl loses her home and family to war, runs into the woods, and is taken in by three witches who feed her hunger for revenge on the warlord who did it. Shakespeare's tragedy unfolds somewhere offstage; The 4th Witch keeps its eye on the child left in the wreckage, and along the way, a taste for blood passes from one generation to the next. It is strange, handmade, and beautiful.ADVISORY  Recommended for ages 12 and up. There are loud sounds and flashing lights.RUN TIME  65 minutes

title: WANTED
description: How far would you go to get everything you ever WANTED?  Texas, 1893 — Twin sisters Mary and Martha Clarke are on the run. The sisters, Black women who pass for white and hide in plain sight, straddle a dangerous line between two Americas. But as powerful forces close in to keep their family from claiming a future of their own, Mary and Martha are driven to desperate measures to save their mother and their family's legacy. When survival demands they do the unthinkable, the sisters nevertheless fight for self-determination, dignity, and the inheritance they have long been denied.  A soulful and dangerous new Broadway musical, WANTED is the mostly true story of Mary and Martha Clarke: sisters, outlaws, legends. This New York Times Critic's Pick has been hailed as "thrillingly original" with an "audacious and rollicking story." The production stars Solea Pfeiffer as Mary, Liisi LaFontaine as Martha, and Grammy® Award winner Ledisi as Tallulah. The Kinfolk, a vibrant chorus of ancestors, guide them forward on an odyssey of sisterhood, rebellion, and freedom.WANTED features book and lyrics by Variety "Star to Watch" Angelica Chéri, a descendant of the Sisters Clarke, and music by Richard Rodgers Award–winning composer Ross Baum. The production is directed by Tony Award® nominee and Obie Award® winner Stevie Walker-Webb, with choreography by Chelsey Arce.                                   On sale NOW through NYUHome!How to Purchase Tickets Online (http://www.nyu.edu/life/resources-and-services/nyu-box-office/ticket-central/faqs/online-ordering-faq.html)YOU MUST PRESENT YOUR NYU ID AND THE CREDIT CARD YOU WILL BE USING TO PURCHASE THESE TICKETS AT NYU BOX OFFICE IN ORDER TO CLAIM YOUR TICKETS. title: Vitalisms II
description: Vitalisms II is an exhibition-as-experiment that continues a long-term research and education project on contemporary painting in China. Following the first chapter's inquiry into the historicity of painting, we now turn toward a different question: How does valuecome into being through our encounters with painting?  As the opening season of our new artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), Vitalisms II considers inheritance as a condition we inhabit and reinterpret. Within the financial imagination, value is rendered calculable, comparable, and exchangeable. Yet value can also name artistic, historical, social, institutional, and affective relations. What happens when a painting is encountered as an artwork, cultural artifact, collectible object, commodity, or financial asset?Vitalisms II focuses on abstract and non-representational painting, a field whose boundaries remain uncertain. The exhibition brings together practices ranging from conceptually driven, hard-edged geometric painting to more intuitive and expressive approaches, including works that approach the threshold of representation. How might abstraction reveal, rather than obscure, relations that are otherwise difficult to perceive? How might we keep interpretation open, rather than seeking settlement? And what might speculation come to mean as a practice of imagining otherwise, rather than predicting return?  The title Vitalisms draws from Isabelle Graw's account of painting's "vitalistic fantasies"—how vitality and agency have been projected onto painting. *Vitalisms I asked whether we could extend these fantasies and think of paintings as active participants in the historical and social relations through which they are made, encountered, and circulated. Vitalisms II asks: What might happen when we approach a painting not simply as an image to be interpreted, but as something with which we enter into relation?  Like the first Vitalisms, this chapter is conceived as an experiment in which knowledge is exchanged and produced throughout the exhibition. During weekly study sessions, we spend extended time with the paintings, developing interpretations collectively through close looking, discussion, and reflection. These encounters become part of the exhibition's research, inviting us to ask: What might we come to value—and, in turn, make possible?  * Isabelle Graw, The Love of Painting (Sternberg Press, 2018): 21-24.——————————————————���——————————————————–Vitalisms II is accompanied by related events, including:  OPENING RECEPTIONFriday, 18 September, 16:00–19:00        A public reception to celebrate the exhibition's opening with food and drinks.STUDY SESSION (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/form-and-content-ii)  Form & Content II: How Do We Value Painting(s)?Fridays, 13:00–14:00 (English) / 16:00–17:00 PM (Chinese)      9, 16, 23, 30 October      6, 13, 20 November        For the artwork featured in each session and the full schedule, please visit the event webpage.  A weekly series of Study Sessions facilitated by ICA curators using Visual Thinking Strategies (VTS). Each one-hour session focuses on a single painting, inviting participants to spend time looking and sharing their observations and interpretations through conversation. The sessions bring the public into Vitalisms II's research into how value comes into being through our encounters with painting. No prior knowledge of art or the exhibition is required.ROUNDTABLE (https://ica.shanghai.nyu.edu/program/after-looking)  After Looking: What Does Looking Have to Do with Value?Saturday, 5 December, 13:30-17:00        A roundtable bringing together the artists exhibiting in Vitalisms II and the ICA curators who facilitated the exhibition's Study Sessions. Over seven weeks, the public spent sustained time with individual paintings through close looking and group discussion. From these sessions, the curators will bring selected observations, interpretations, and questions into conversation with the artists, exploring how paintings acquire meaning and value through different encounters.  All events are FREE and OPEN to the public.  For further details and to register for events, please visit the event pages under Related programs below.  —————————���———————————————————————��———–  The exhibition Vitalisms II and related events are presented as the first season of the ICA's artistic research program Untimely Inheritances (2026–28), attending to what inheritance asks of us and how we might inhabit unfinished worlds through practices of interpretation, response, and transformation.Vitalisms II is organized by Michelle Yeonho Hyun with BAO Yang and CHEN Baichao, with additional support by HOU Chuchu, QU Yanqiu and JIAO Meiqi. Special thanks to Arts & Collections Foundation, Luoying Sheng, Han Xiao, and Chong Zhou for their generosity, as well as Antenna Space, CLC Gallery, Magician Space, Ota Fine Arts, ShanghART Gallery and ZIAN Gallery, for their support. Graphic Design by LIU Anqi. Exhibition Design by FANG Yuan.  Our deepest gratitude belongs to the artists for sharing their knowledge, work, and time with us, extending our curiosity and creating more questions.  Early research and development for Untimely Inheritances received kind support from Goethe-Institut, as well as research assistance from Oviya Dinakhar, Fay Guan, and Lizzy Xie.
