title: Urban Farm Volunteers
description:
Volunteer with our team to manage our one-acre Urban Farm! 
Whether you are new to our farm or have been a tried-and-true weekly volunteer, come and join us! Our farmers have a lot of farm chores and composting to do weekly and you can help us take care of this important urban educational agricultural resource. 
On Sundays we not only do farm chores, but we are joined by the NYC Compost Project with Big Reuse who help us manage our 5-bin compost system to create much needed organic matter for our planting beds! 
Individuals under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an adult who volunteers with them. Individuals ages 16 & 17 can volunteer if a parent or guardian has signed a waiver. Please find a downloadable waiver here: Waiver for unaccompanied 16 & 17 year olds 
This volunteer event is for individuals from the community and not open to groups larger than 5 people. If you wish to bring more than 5 people, you must first contact us at volunteers@randallsisland.org. 
New volunteers must register for this event here. 
Location: Urban Farm 
For inquiries about accessibility, to request accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

title: Wild Oyster Survey
description:
Wild oysters are a key indicator of ecosystem health in the New York Harbor. Randall’s Island Park Alliance is partnering with the Billion Oyster Project to conduct a wild oyster survey in the Little Hell Gate Salt Marsh.  
Volunteers will have the opportunity to identify oysters and take multiple parameters to determine the abundance, size, and health of the wild oyster population. Be sure to wear clothing and footwear you don’t mind getting muddy! Volunteers will meet at the entrance to the Little Hell Gate Salt Marsh near the Asphalt Pad.  
Registration is required here. 
Location: Little Hell Gate Salt Marsh 
For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

title: Team RIVER Volunteers
description:
Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome! 
This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.org 
Volunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s Island 
Registration is required here. 
Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration. 
For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

Location: Urban Farm

title: Recycled Plates: An Introduction to Intaglio Etching
description:
This workshop introduces participants to intaglio printmaking through the use of recycled Tetrapak cartons as printing plates. Participants will learn how to incise designs into the plates and create small editions of prints using a small 3D tabletop etching press. This is a great introduction to printing with Tetra Pak! 
Materials Included

description: Delve into the storied past of distilled spirits in Brooklyn with Fort Hamilton Distillery and our neighbors at Green-Wood Cemetery.

title: Industry City Gourmet Food and Drinks Tour
description:
Set against the iconic backdrop of Sunset Park’s historic waterfront, the massive, revitalized structures of Industry City form a breathtaking stage for an exclusive culinary journey. This premium food and cocktail tour is a curated exploration of taste and craft, transforming an evening into a memorable, high-end experience. 
Your adventure begins with artistic bonbons at Lilac Chocolates, explores gourmet imports at Sahadi’s, and includes a refined whiskey tasting at Fort Hamilton Distillery, followed by a sophisticated sake flight. Savor additional artisanal discoveries within the awe-inspiring industrial halls. 
Perfect as a distinctive date night, this tour is also fully customizable for private groups and corporate retreats. We specialize in tailoring this engaging experience for team-building and client entertainment, making it an ideal one-day corporate outing. A sophisticated mini-vacation for locals and a profound discovery for visitors.

title: Collage Workshop
description: Join us for a collage workshop led by Laura Salvatore and leave with a masterpiece made with all reused materials!

title: Warm Sake Tasting Class and Brewery Tour
description:
Exploring sake temperature and pairing — warm sake, done right, is a revelation. 
For a long time, warm sake has gotten a bad rap! But it can be absolutely delicious when you pick the right sake and the right temperature. Join us for this exciting exploration of sake temperature and the joys of warming sake — the perfect way to explore the subtle umami and richness of premium sake. 
We’ll contrast chilled sake with the same sake served warm, and enjoy carefully selected food pairings to round out the tasting flight. In all, we’ll taste five kinds of sake, each paired with a delicious bite to bring out the flavors and textures. As always, this class includes a behind-the-scenes brewery tour to see how sake is made at NY State’s first sake brewery.

description:

description:

title: Movie Screening of Prince - Sign O' the Times
description:
Get It Right Music in association with BK One Productions is proud to present our late summer/early fall music documentary and horror film movies (yes, those two things go together, and yes, we ARE wondering why you are asking!). Watch fan favorites on our 16-foot wide LED video wall and enjoy the film in full concert sound! 
Sign o’ the Times is a 1987 American concert film directed by, scored by, and starring Prince. The film features the band that accompanied Prince on the 1987 Sign o’ the Times Tour: dancer Cat Glover, keyboardist Boni Boyer, bassist Levi Seacer Jr., guitarist Miko Weaver, drummer Sheila E., keyboardist Doctor Fink, and the horn section of Eric Leeds and Atlanta Bliss; Wally Safford and Greg Brooks (of The Bodyguards from the Revolution era) reprised their roles as dancers, vocalists and comic foils. 
Event Info
Film: Prince – Sign O’ the Times
Date: October 15th, 2026
Doors: 7:00pm
Screening: 7:30pm
RSVP: Free or strongly encourage guaranteed $20 two-drink included RSVP. 
Address: Industry City Bandshell Stage, Courtyard 1/2 at Industry City in Brooklyn, New York between 36th and 37th street and 2nd and 3rd Avenues.
ENTER 238 36th Street, Brooklyn, NY on your GPS device 
The selection of music documentaries was curated by audience vote from our summer concert series and the horror movies came from out of our brains!
Seating for these screenings are limited to 150 people or so (with slightly more for the music docs so peeps can throw down appropriately.
Fans who purchase the 2 drink guaranteed RSVP will be guaranteed entry, natch! So you will save money at the bar, AND make sure you aren’t shut out!
This event is free with RSVP, ages 8 and up are welcome. There will be drink specials, all night, as well.
Limited seating (about 100-125 seats), tons of standing room. No strollers.
No outside beverages. There will be drink specials all night long from our courtyard bar.
While we do our best to gauge the number of RSVPs, entry is still on a first-come, first-served basis, so please arrive early! Once we hit capacity, we will only let people in on an in and out basis! Fans who purchase the 2 drink RSVP at check-out will be guaranteed entry!
The venue is located in an open-air courtyard featuring a full concert sound stage. Fans can get affordable drinks from the venue’s bar and order food from over 17 options inside the adjoining food hall. 
How to get here:
Take the D, N, R lines to 36th street station in Brooklyn and walk west one block to Industry City. 3 stops from Manhattan. 30 minutes from Herald Square.
From Long Island, take the LIRR to Atlantic Terminal then take the D, N or R train to 36th street.

description: Welcome to Brooklyn Kura! Join us for a tour of our state-of-the-art sake brewery in Industry City, Brooklyn. title: Monoprinting with Gelli Plates
description:
This workshop will introduce adults to the possibilities of monoprinting with Gelli plates. Participants will explore techniques including layering transparent colors, creating textures, and building compositions through repetition and variation. This process-based workshop welcomes beginners and offers experienced artists an opportunity to expand their printmaking practice through experimentation and intuitive image-making with accessible gelli printing. These prints can stand alone or be used for further printing with block printing.. 
Materials Included

title: Sloppy Heads, Chris Forsyth's What is Now, Wet Tuna
description:
Industry City and Get It Right Music in association with Murmrr Presents are happy to present a stacked triple bill including Sloppy Heads, Chris Forsyth’s What is Now, and Wet Tuna! 
Event Info
Date: October 17th, 2026
Doors: 3:00pm
Show: 4:00-7:00pm
Tickets: $15 per person plus fees
The first 50 people to buy tickets get a free 12-ounce beer, well drink, 6 ounce wine or N/A beverage. 
Address: Industry City Bandshell Stage, Courtyard 1/2 at Industry City in Brooklyn New York between 36th and 37th street and 2nd and 3rd Avenues.
ENTER 238 36th Street, Brooklyn, NY on your GPS device 
The venue is located in an open-air courtyard featuring a full concert sound stage. Fans can get affordable drinks from the venue’s bar and order food from over 17 options inside the adjoining food hall. Concert is rain or shine. 
How to get here:
Take the D, N, R lines to 36th street station in Brooklyn and walk west one block to Industry City. 3 stops from Manhattan. 30 minutes from Herald Square.
From Long Island, take the LIRR to Atlantic Terminal then take the D, N or R train to 36th street. 
More about the bands:
THE SLOPPY HEADS!
Thrill to the electrifying guitar wizardry of Jimmy Jumpjump!
Gasp at the audacity of the legendary Ariella Stok aka Starmaiden to whom shame is but a word in the dictionary!
Grope to the exotic jungle rhythms of Bill the Drummer!
In one of their sought after East Coast appearances since the release of their second album, Sometimes Just One Second on Shrimper Records.
Bop on down to see them perform live in concert, where anything can happen and usually does. Fun for kids from 2 to 82. 
Chris Forsyth’s WHAT IS NOW is a new collaborative project from Philadelphia guitarist Chris Forsyth (BASIC, Solar Motel Band) featuring double bassist John Moran (Bark Culture, Daniel Villareal Trio) and drummer Joey Sullivan (Florry, Bark Culture).
Together they create spontaneous song forms exploring lyrically ambient moods, repetition, rhythmic interplay, and a mindful leaderless-ness. As suggested by the players’ pedigrees, elements or motorik propulsion, trance jazz, and deconstructed rock moves abound.
The Bandcamp- and merch table-only CD “Both / And” is the debut release, about which Laura Snapes wrote this in the Guardian: “The Philadelphia guitarist swaps his usual Television-indebted questing riffage for 25 minutes of tingly, exploratory improv alongside double bassist John Moran and drummer Joey Sullivan: imagine a scruffier Necks.” 
WET TUNA was formed for all beings. Legendary DJ/HEAD Jeff Conklin says “revel in the earth/space magic!” Their new record is called “VAST”. Matt “MV” Valentine with Jim Bliss & Erika Elder are the triad. They specialize in homegrown dubwise song exploration.
The kaleidoscopic sonic agriculture of Wet Tuna has long inhabited its own universe. Over the past five years, they have established themselves as one of the most forward thinking and anarchic of the many groups rethinking and reconceptualizing the notion of the “jam band,” all the while frustrating critical attempts to slot the group’s music into any scene, sound, or easily classifiable genre fad.
There remains a beautiful simplicity at the core of MV’s workbench alchemy; as with the music of Can, there is in his productions almost always a lodestar fixed within the eye of whatever maelstrom or fragmented primal abstractions surround it. On Warping All By Yourself, funk and soul are both the unifying principles and the unlikely bedrocks upon which everything else orbits and rests, resulting in a concoction of iconoclastic, free-dancing music that has as much in common with Funkadelic as it does Crazy Horse.

More about REPRISE
REPRISE, a band formed to reprise the Phish experience, is itself an all-star band. Cal Kehoe, longtime frontman for Pink Talking Fish, helms the enterprise on guitar. Adrian Tramontano (Twiddle, Kung Fu and The Breakfast) masters the drums. Scott Chasolen chairs the boards for the project, bringing years of experience as a founding member of Ulu and keyboardist of internationally touring Pink Floyd tribute The Machine. Multi-instrumentalist and composer Chris DeAngelis (The Machine, Kung Fu, and The Breakfast) rounds out the foursome on bass. The time is near, the mission’s clear.

title: Family Program: Handmade Stationery Block Printing
description:
In this hands-on family workshop, participants will explore the fundamentals of relief printmaking while creating a personalized family stationery set. Families will learn simple stamping and printing techniques, carve their own designs, and experiment with everyday materials like vegetables and found objects to make unique prints. A selection of pre-carved blocks will also be available, allowing participants to combine personal designs with existing imagery and explore the possibilities of shared printmaking tools. 
Materials Included
Adults & Children 6+

title: Industry City Gourmet Food and Drinks Tour
description:
Set against the iconic backdrop of Sunset Park’s historic waterfront, the massive, revitalized structures of Industry City form a breathtaking stage for an exclusive culinary journey. This premium food and cocktail tour is a curated exploration of taste and craft, transforming an evening into a memorable, high-end experience. 
Your adventure begins with artistic bonbons at Lilac Chocolates, explores gourmet imports at Sahadi’s, and includes a refined whiskey tasting at Fort Hamilton Distillery, followed by a sophisticated sake flight. Savor additional artisanal discoveries within the awe-inspiring industrial halls. 
Perfect as a distinctive date night, this tour is also fully customizable for private groups and corporate retreats. We specialize in tailoring this engaging experience for team-building and client entertainment, making it an ideal one-day corporate outing. A sophisticated mini-vacation for locals and a profound discovery for visitors.
